main_body: Tile-roofed timber-frame barn/farmhouse: a large red-orange tiled roof with a half-timbered dormer, over a plaster front wall with a big double wooden door and two small windows
top_band: Roof slope rows ~1-53: a cream highlight ridge row at rows 3-4, then orange/maroon scalloped tiles down to the eave at rows ~50-53; a dark eave line at rows 54-56
evidence: Reading a column through the middle: the dark ridge edge, cream highlight row, then many rows of scalloped roof tiles, ending at a lighter orange eave row. Directly under it is a dark shadow band (rows 54-56), then the plaster and door front face from row ~57 to 89. The roof is a large visible sloped surface with a distinct front edge and eave shadow, and the wall is a separate vertical face with an inset door and window frames. This is the same structure as the Beodeul house references.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 tone steps (cream highlight, light orange, orange, maroon, dark purple) with per-tile scallops. The plaster has speckle dots. The timber is shaded in several browns, with a patterned door, small windows and a flower box. The outlines are dark brown or purple, tinted to match the neighbouring material, and are not black stickers. The stone base is grey with variation. Detail and density match the reference houses.
